title: Sierra Nevada & Las Alpujarras
subRegion: Andalucía — Sierra Nevada National Park & the Alpujarra Granadina

bestPeriod.avoid: July–August (38 °C+ in the villages, acequias switched to irrigation, no shade below 2,000 m); December–April (high summits snowbound, Hoya del Portillo road closed)

accommodation.note: Alpujarra guesthouses €55–€95 dbl/night; Refugio Poqueira dorm ~€20, half-board ~€38–€48

food.note: Menú del día €12–€16; tapas free with drinks in Granada province

transport.note: Rental car 7 days €190–€300, fuel, plus the national park high-mountain shuttle

activities.note: Park shuttle bus, refuge night, Alhambra ticket if you add Granada

profile.difficultyNote: 4/5 — the running is rarely technical but you climb 2,000 m in a day to 3,479 m, in dry heat, on exposed ground

gatewayAirport: GRX — Granada Federico García Lorca (1 h 15 to Capileira); AGP — Málaga is 2 h 15 and usually has better fares
summary: This week runs the biggest vertical relief in Western Europe outside the Alps: from white Berber-plan villages at 1,050 m to Mulhacén at 3,479 m, the highest ground on the Iberian mainland, in a single climb. The Alpujarra south slope gives you terraced chestnut and almond terrain threaded by *acequias* — Moorish snowmelt channels that double as the region's only reliable water — while the Granada north side gives the Vereda de la Estrella, a long, cool, glacial-valley approach to the north faces. The arc is deliberate: two acclimatisation days on the GR-7 and the acequia paths, a refuge night at 2,500 m, the Mulhacén day, a genuine recovery day in the gorge at Monachil, then a high traverse to finish. It suits a runner who is more worried about heat and altitude than about scrambling.

itinerary.title: Arrive, and the Poqueira village triangle
itinerary.morning: Fly into Granada (GRX) or Málaga, collect the car, and drive up the Lecrín valley and the Órgiva road to **Capileira** (1,436 m). Buy food — the villages have small shops that close 14:00–17:30.
itinerary.afternoon: Easy orientation loop on the GR-7 down through **Bubión** to **Pampaneira** and back up the Poqueira barranco path — 300 m of descent and the same back up, on cobbles and terrace paths, with the acequia channels running beside you.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **El Corral del Castaño** in Capileira — plato alpujarreño, migas, and a Contraviesa red.
itinerary.dayStats: 10 km / 480 m D+ / ~60% cobbled village path / 1 h 20–1 h 50; transfer 1 h 15 from GRX.

itinerary.title: GR-7 to Trevélez
itinerary.morning: Run the **GR-7 east** from Capileira through **Pitres, Pórtugos** (stop at the iron-red **Fuente Agria**) and **Busquístar**, dropping into and out of the Trevélez river gorge on old mule paths through chestnut terraces.
itinerary.afternoon: Finish in **Trevélez** (1,476 m), one of the highest permanently inhabited villages in Spain. Taxi or pre-positioned second car back, or run the high acequia return for a 34 km day.
itinerary.evening: Eat at **Mesón La Fragua** in Trevélez — jamón de Trevélez cured at altitude, and choto al ajillo.
itinerary.dayStats: 21 km / 1,050 m D+ / 950 m D- / ITRA 2 / 2 h 45–3 h 45 / 5 village fountains en route.

itinerary.title: Climb to Refugio Poqueira and sleep at 2,500 m
itinerary.morning: Leave Capileira at 08:00 on the **Cebadillas path** up the Poqueira barranco — pine plantation, then open high pasture, following the río to the **Refugio Poqueira (2,500 m)**, 84 places and staffed year-round.
itinerary.afternoon: Deliberately easy: a 5 km reconnaissance jog toward the **Río Mulhacén** and back for altitude exposure, then rest, hydrate and eat early. Do not chase the summit today.
itinerary.evening: Refuge half-board — lentil stew and a communal table full of Spanish mountaineers who will tell you exactly what the snow line is doing.
itinerary.dayStats: 11.5 km / 1,100 m D+ / 2 h–2 h 45 plus a 5 km shakeout; sleeping at 2,500 m.

itinerary.title: Mulhacén, 3,479 m
itinerary.morning: Out of the refuge by 06:30. Climb to the **Laguna de la Caldera** (3,050 m), then the west flank onto the **Mulhacén summit at 3,479 m** — the highest point on the Iberian mainland, with the Alcazaba and the 700 m north face falling away on the other side.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend the broad south ridge to **Alto del Chorrillo** and pick up the track to **Hoya del Portillo**, then the forest descent to Capileira. Long, hot and relentless — save water for the last hour.
itinerary.evening: Recovery beers and tapas in Capileira; in Granada province the tapa comes free with the drink.
itinerary.dayStats: 24 km / 1,050 m up / 2,050 m down / high point 3,479 m / 4 h 30–6 h / zero water after the Caldera.

itinerary.title: Recovery day at Los Cahorros de Monachil
itinerary.morning: Drive north over the Puerto de la Ragua or round via Granada to **Monachil**. Run the **Los Cahorros** gorge loop — 8 km of hanging bridges, a cabled rock traverse and a tunnel beside the Río Monachil, cool and shaded the whole way.
itinerary.afternoon: Nothing strenuous. Granada: the Albaicín, a long lunch, and free tapas on Calle Navas. Optional cold-water soak in the river.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Granada; return to the Alpujarra or overnight in the city.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km / 350 m D+ / ITRA 3 (bridges and cables) / 1 h–1 h 20 / total drive ~1 h 45 each way.

itinerary.title: Vereda de la Estrella, the north side
itinerary.morning: Drive to **Güéjar Sierra** and the Barranco de San Juan trailhead. Run the **Vereda de la Estrella** — the old mining track along the Genil, under chestnut and holm oak, with the **Mulhacén and Alcazaba north walls** opening ahead — to Cueva Secreta and back.
itinerary.afternoon: Extend to the **Cortijo de la Estrella** ruins if legs allow, then drive back over the Sierra to Capileira for the last night; stop at the **Hoya de la Mora** (2,500 m) viewpoint for the Veleta.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Mesón Poqueira in Capileira — soup, grilled meat, and an early night.
itinerary.dayStats: 18 km out-and-back / 700 m D+ / 2 h 15–3 h / two stream fords / no signal in the valley.

itinerary.title: Veleta and out
itinerary.morning: Early drive to **Hoya de la Mora** (2,500 m) above the ski station and run the old road and ridge to **Veleta (3,396 m)** — the fastest 3,000 m summit in Spain, with the Alpujarra, the Mediterranean and, on the clearest mornings, the Rif of Morocco visible together.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend, drive to Granada or Málaga, and eat properly before the flight.
itinerary.dayStats: 17 km / 950 m D+ / high point 3,396 m / 2 h 15–3 h; 45 min drive to Granada.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Real de Poqueira
accommodationStrategy.description: Right in the middle of Capileira at 1,436 m, so both the GR-7 and the Poqueira barranco start from the door and you never move the car on running days. Small pool, parking, and breakfast from 08:00 (ask for a bag earlier). €65–€95 double outside August.

accommodationStrategy.name: Refugio Poqueira
accommodationStrategy.description: The only shelter on the south high mountain and the key to doing Mulhacén sanely: sleeping at 2,500 m turns a brutal 1,750 m ascent into a manageable 1,050 m one and gives you real acclimatisation. 84 places, open all year, half-board available; book directly by phone or its own site.

accommodationStrategy.name: Finca Los Llanos
accommodationStrategy.style: garden hotel on the edge of Capileira
accommodationStrategy.description: Quieter, with a pool, terrace and parking, and better for the recovery half of the week. Five minutes from the village centre, with space to spread wet kit. Similar price band, worth the swap after the refuge night.

logistics.connectivity: Spain is EU; roaming at domestic rates. Movistar has the best mountain coverage. **No signal in the Poqueira barranco floor, in the Vereda de la Estrella valley or in Los Cahorros.** Download offline maps and the park's shuttle timetable before leaving Capileira.
logistics.emergency: **112**; the Guardia Civil's GREIM mountain unit covers Sierra Nevada and is based at Pinos Genil. Rescue in Andalucía is not routinely billed to the casualty, but insurance covering activity above 3,000 m is still sensible. Give your route to the refuge guardian before summit days.
logistics.weather: The defining phenomena are the **terral** (a hot, dry down-slope wind that can push village temperatures past 40 °C) and sudden high-mountain cloud that drops visibility on the Mulhacén–Veleta crest with almost no warning. Afternoon thunderstorms build over the summits from June. Snow and névé can persist in the Caldera and on the Veleta north side into early July.
logistics.bookingWindows: **Refugio Poqueira** and the **national park high-mountain shuttle** (Servicio de Interpretación de Altas Cumbres, Capileira to Mirador de Trevélez) both need advance booking and both fill on summer weekends — reserve 2–4 weeks out. The Alhambra needs weeks. Ultra Sierra Nevada entries open months before its early-summer date.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards work in hotels and most restaurants; carry €100 cash for village bars, the refuge and the shuttle. Tipping is minimal — round up or leave 5%.
logistics.transportRules: A car is effectively required; Alsa buses reach Capileira and Trevélez but only once or twice a day. The A-44 and A-92 are toll-free. The **Hoya del Portillo forest road above Capileira is gated seasonally** and the last section to the high mountain is closed to private vehicles — the park shuttle is the legal way up. Ski-station road to Hoya de la Mora is open and free in summer.
logistics.permits: Sierra Nevada National Park has **no entry fee and no running permit**, but the high zone above roughly 2,700 m has restricted vehicle access and camping rules: bivouacking is permitted above 2,500 m from sunset to sunrise only, with tents pitched no earlier than an hour before dusk. Drones need park authorisation. Fires are banned outright.
logistics.health: Village tap water is potable. **Acequia water is irrigation water** — treat it, or drink only from named fountains. Real risks here are heat exhaustion, sunburn at altitude and dehydration, not falls. Snakes (Montpellier, ladder snake) are harmless to humans. There is no avalanche concern in the recommended season, but check the park's snow report before any pre-June summit attempt.

proTips: **Use the park shuttle as an uphill lift, not a tour.** Book the Capileira bus to the Mirador de Trevélez (about 2,700 m), run Mulhacén from there and descend on foot to the village — you get the summit at a third of the climbing cost, and it is the only motorised access allowed.
**Book the refuge night before you book flights.** Refugio Poqueira is the difference between a good Mulhacén day and an altitude-headache slog, and its 84 places go on summer weekends.

**Time the week to the acequia charge.** The channels above Capileira run hardest in the six weeks after the main snowmelt, roughly mid-May to late June — that's when the mountain is greenest and water is everywhere.
**Take the second car to Trevélez.** The GR-7 point-to-point is far better run one-way; a €40 taxi or a shuttled second car buys you the whole traverse instead of an out-and-back.
**Run Veleta on your last morning, not your first.** It's the easiest 3,000 m in Spain but only if you have already slept high — done cold on day one it will cost you the rest of the week.
**Eat the tapas system.** In Granada province and much of the Alpujarra, each drink comes with a substantial free tapa. Three beers is dinner, for about €9.

**Cool down in Los Cahorros deliberately.** The Monachil gorge is 15 °C cooler than the south-facing Alpujarra slopes and the river pools are a legitimate recovery tool between the Mulhacén and Veleta days.
**Watch for the Ultra Sierra Nevada weekend.** Race week fills every bed in Güéjar Sierra and Capileira — either enter it, or avoid it.

raw.Signature routes: (1) **Mulhacén from Capileira** via Hoya del Portillo (2,150 m), Alto del Chorrillo and the Mirador de Trevélez: 26 km, 1,750 m D+ to **3,479 m**, mid-pack 4 h 30–6 h; shortened to 14 km / 900 m by taking the park shuttle to the Mirador. (2) **Refugio Poqueira (2,500 m) from Capileira** by the Cebadillas/Río Naute path: 11.5 km, 1,100 m D+, 2 h–2 h 45. (3) **Veleta (3,396 m) from the Hoya de la Mora** (2,500 m): 17 km, 950 m D+, 2 h 15–3 h. (4) **Vereda de la Estrella** from the Barranco de San Juan to Cueva Secreta, under the Mulhacén–Alcazaba north walls: 18 km out-and-back, 700 m D+, 2 h 15–3 h. (5) **Los Cahorros de Monachil gorge loop**: 8 km, 350 m D+, 1 h–1 h 20. (6) **GR-7 village link, Pampaneira–Bubión–Capileira–Pitres–Pórtugos–Busquístar–Trevélez**: 21 km, 1,050 m D+, 2 h 45–3 h 45.
raw.Technicality (ITRA-style 1–5; 1 = fire r: GR-7 and acequia paths **2**. Mulhacén by the normal south route **2**, mostly a rideable gravel track and broad ridge — the altitude, not the terrain, is the difficulty. Veleta ridge **3** on loose micaschist blocks. Vereda de la Estrella **2–3** with two stream crossings. Los Cahorros **3** — hanging bridges, a cable traverse and a low tunnel. Nothing here needs hands except by choice.
raw.Terrain split, week average: ~30% stony mule track and cobbled village path, ~25% high-mountain gravel road (the old Veleta road and the Hoya del Portillo track), ~20% micaschist scree and blocky ridge above 2,800 m, ~15% terraced almond/chestnut singletrack, ~10% forest fire road in the Poqueira pine plantation. Dry, abrasive, dusty — sand gaiters earn their place.
raw.Waymarking: **GR-7 (part of E4)** in red-and-white; **PR-A** local routes in yellow-and-white; national park boards at Hoya del Portillo, Alto del Chorrillo and the Poqueira refuge junction. High above 2,800 m the marking thins to cairns and painted dots — the Mulhacén–Veleta crest is navigated by feature, not by paint.
raw.Water refill points and month reliabilit: *Acequias* are the system: the **Acequia Alta and Acequia Baja above Capileira** and the **Acequia de Mecina** flow strongly **April–June** on snowmelt, are switched to field irrigation in July–August (channels can run dry or foul), and refill with autumn rain from late September. Named fixed points: **village fountains at Capileira, Bubión, Pampaneira, Trevélez, Pórtugos (the ferruginous Fuente Agria) and Busquístar** — potable year-round. **Refugio Poqueira** — water and drinks all year, hut open year-round. **Río Mulhacén and Laguna de la Caldera** — snowmelt, filter or treat, reliable to about mid-July then thin. **Nothing at all on the Hoya del Portillo–Alto del Chorrillo track**: carry 2 L for the Mulhacén day.
raw.Navigation: Editorial Penibética 1:40,000 "Sierra Nevada" and 1:25,000 "Alta Montaña" sheets; GPX from Wikiloc (dense Spanish coverage), the Ultra Sierra Nevada course files, and the park's Ventana del Visitante portal. Coverage: good in villages and on summits, **dead in the Poqueira barranco bottom, in the Vereda de la Estrella valley and in Los Cahorros**. Bail-outs: the Poqueira refuge is staffed all year and is the only shelter on the south side; from the Veleta ridge, the old road drops to Hoya de la Mora; from the Vereda, the only exit is back down the valley.
raw.Recovery, altitude and heat: Day 5 is a true low day. This is the only trip in the region where **altitude genuinely matters**: 3,479 m after sleeping at 1,436 m is a real dose, hence the refuge night at 2,500 m first. Start every summit day by 06:30 — the south slope has zero shade after 09:00 — and carry 500 ml/hour above 2,500 m in June. Expect 3–4 °C at dawn at the refuge even when the village is 25 °C.

sources.verified: Refugio Poqueira sits at 2,500 m, has 84 places and is open year round with half-board available; Mulhacén 3,479 m and Veleta 3,396 m as the two highest Iberian mainland summits; Sierra Nevada is a UTMB-index race venue (Ultra Sierra Nevada, ~100 km with roughly 6,200 m of ascent, plus shorter distances); GRX and AGP transfer times.
sources.confidenceNotes: Re-verify (a) **Refugio Poqueira current nightly and half-board prices** — the figures circulating online date from 2022 and Federación Andaluza rates change annually; (b) **the national park high-mountain shuttle's operating dates, route ends and fare**, which shift year to year and are sometimes suspended; (c) **exact Ultra Sierra Nevada 2026/2027 dates and the distance ladder**; (d) **acequia flow status in the travel month** — irrigation scheduling is set locally and cannot be assumed; (e) **Hoya del Portillo gate status and the snow line on Mulhacén** before any pre-June trip; (f) current guesthouse price bands in Capileira and Trevélez.
